newsitem.title: UK: Three companies in running for UK West Coast rail.
newsitem.headline: Three companies in running for UK West Coast rail.

text.p: Richard Branson's Virgin Group and Sea Containers Ltd said on Thursday they had been shortlisted to operate the Intercity West Coast Ltd UK passenger rail line.

Stagecoach Holdings Plc said earlier it had been shortlisted to make a formal bid for the route, among other lines, taking to three the number of companies in the running for the important West Coast franchise.
Sea Containers said in a statement that 14 companies had expressed interest in the franchise, but railways regulator Opraf had narrowed the list to three.
A Virgin spokesman said, "We are obviously delighted as this news comes on the back of our recent selection as preferred bidder on the Cross Country franchise."
"We look forward to putting some very exciting proposals in for the West Coast," the spokesman added.

Sea Containers president James Sherwood said substantial economIes could be achieved by combining the 48 train sets of Intercity West Coast with the 40 Sea Containers operates on its existing Great North Eastern Railway franchise.
He said Opraf had indicated that final proposals were due early next year and the business would be transferred to the new operator in the spring.
The West Coast line operates some 700 route miles, mainly between London and Birmingham and London and northwest England and Glasgow in Scotland.
